title: Heat capacity of a solid falls at low temperature
caption: Classically every solid has C = 3R per mole (Dulong–Petit). Quantised vibrations freeze out when k_BT is small compared with ħω: in the Einstein model C/3R = x²eˣ/(eˣ − 1)², x = θ_E/T. Diamond's vibrations are stiff (θ near 1300 K), so at room temperature it sits well below 3R (about 0.25 on this curve).
alt: Heat capacity as a fraction of 3R against temperature over the Einstein temperature, rising from zero in an S-shape towards 1.
description: At T = θ_E: 0.921. At T = 2θ_E: 0.979, near the classical value.
At low temperature it falls off exponentially; the Debye model, with a spread of frequencies, gives the observed T³ instead.
